subsystems.name: Micro-bot platform
subsystems.role: the mobile unit itself, small enough to move through drains, wall cavities and pavement joints.

subsystems.name: Onboard power
subsystems.role: no battery of that size lasts long, so energy must be scavenged or delivered.
parts: wireless power pickup from street furniture

subsystems.name: Swarm communication and localisation
subsystems.role: bots must know where they are and what their neighbours are doing, without GPS indoors or underground.
parts: shared map held by the swarm, not one robot

subsystems.name: Distributed control
subsystems.role: no central controller can command millions of units, so tasks are allocated locally.
parts: stigmergic markers left in the environment
fault detection that routes around dead units

subsystems.name: Inspection sensing
subsystems.role: finding a defect before it becomes a failure.

subsystems.name: Repair and cleaning payload
subsystems.role: doing the work once a defect is found.

subsystems.name: Depots
subsystems.role: somewhere to recharge, refill consumables and hand back data.
parts: docking stations in lamp posts, manholes or utility cabinets
data uplink to a municipal asset-management system

buildSteps.title: Define the maintenance tasks worth automating
buildSteps.detail: Inspection of bridge bearings, sewer joint sealing or facade cleaning are candidates; each sets the size, payload and power budget of the bot.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the micro-bots
buildSteps.detail: Silicon micromachining, printed circuit assembly and micro-moulding are combined into a body a few centimetres across; batteries and sensors are integrated under cleanroom conditions.

buildSteps.title: Write the swarm behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Algorithms are developed in simulation first, then validated on small batches of tens to hundreds of physical robots in a test arena.

buildSteps.title: Build the depots
buildSteps.detail: Docking and refill points are installed at fixed intervals across the city, wired into existing power and data ducts.

buildSteps.title: Map and instrument the city
buildSteps.detail: Assets are surveyed and a shared digital model is built so the swarm knows what 'normal' looks like and where to go.

buildSteps.title: Deploy in a controlled district
buildSteps.detail: One neighbourhood is covered first, with humans verifying every repair and rescuing failed bots.

buildSteps.title: Close the human loop down
buildSteps.detail: As reliability rises, bots are trusted to act on routine defects and escalate only unusual ones.

buildSteps.title: Scale to city level
buildSteps.detail: Depots, manufacturing and fleet management are expanded until coverage is continuous rather than campaign-based.

prerequisites.why: laboratory robots of this size move, but slowly and on flat ground, and cannot yet climb or burrow reliably.
the energy needed to carry a tool and work on a surface is far more than these bots can store.
laboratory swarms of tens to a few hundred robots build simple structures; coordination at a million units is unproven.
robots working in sewers, walls and under bridges need alternative positioning that works indoors and underground.
curing sealants, applying coatings and assessing structural safety without a human are all unresolved.

pathway.milestone: laboratory swarms that assemble simple structures, and single inspection robots in sewers and pipelines
pathway.unlocks: proof that coordination and autonomous inspection are possible at small scale.

pathway.milestone: fleets of a few hundred inspection robots working one asset type, such as a tunnel or a bridge
pathway.unlocks: routine autonomous condition monitoring and lower-cost surveys.

pathway.milestone: hybrid crews of humans and robots doing limited repairs in a single district
pathway.unlocks: regulatory and safety experience with robots acting on public infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: self-organising micro-bot fleets maintaining a whole city's surfaces
pathway.unlocks: continuous, invisible upkeep — if power, reliability and accountability problems are solved.
